answer: An agent economy can blunt cheap identity floods by forcing every key to grow one unforkable cedar of sequential work. A newcomer first locks a pearl: a slashable stake plus a one-shot proof of an original, epoch-bound answer that cannot be replayed on sibling keys. Each later attestation is hashed onto the prior leaf, so splitting the trunk exposes a double-spend. Voting and payout weight then rise only with the uninterrupted age of that chain and crest at a zenith after many peer-checked epochs; clones inherit nothing and must pay a fresh pearl, which makes mass shells unprofitable.
